title: Sanitize auth dependencies and optimize token verification path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Multiple services reported elevated risk surface from transitive crypto and SSO transitive libraries during a routine supply-chain audit. Current stack spans OpenSSL 1.1.x bindings, an older JWT library (jose-go v2), and python-saml/xmlsec adapters that require fragile native binaries. Scope: 1) Upgrade core crypto to OpenSSL 3.x-compatible build and ensure FIPS-mode compatibility gating, 2) Replace/lock JWT/OAuth parsing library to one that enforces algorithm whitelisting and strict lifetime/nbf checks, 3) Remove xmlsec native dependency by integrating a native SAML verifier shim (lightweight), 4) Add runtime public-key cache and key-rotation hooks to reduce signature verification latency and make key rotation safer, 5) Add CI gating, SBOM generation, and supply-chain scanning for signed artifacts. Success metrics: - Zero critical CVEs from auth stack after upgrades; - <5% p99 token verification latency regression (goal: net 15% improvement with caching); - All services pass security review and automated SBOM checks.

decision: Adopt OpenSSL 3.0.8 ABI-compatible shim in runtime images and migrate to go-jwt v4 for all Go services. Introduce a lightweight native SAML verifier to remove xmlsec native binary dependency. Maintain a short-lived compatibility layer for legacy HS256 tokens behind a runtime feature flag; require rollout plan for clients to rotate to RS256 within 12 weeks.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for new JWT parsing, algorithm restrictions, and strict time checks. 2) Integration tests for SSO flows with multiple SAML IdP samples. 3) Fuzz tests targeting token header/parsing to catch alg confusion attacks. 4) Performance benchmarks simulating production token rates, measuring p50/p95/p99. 5) SBOM generation and dependency-scan gating in CI; block merge on critical CVEs.
acceptance_criteria: All services build with OpenSSL 3.x runtime image and pass unit/integration tests
JWT library replaced and configured; alg-whitelist enforced in production config
Public-key cache implemented and benchmarked showing no regression at p99 compared to baseline
SAML flow passes end-to-end in staging without xmlsec native binary present
CI pipeline emits SBOM and dependency scan; no critical/high CVEs allowed in dependency tree
Security review completed and signed off by security team
notes: Trade-offs: Removing xmlsec reduces attack surface and supply-chain risk but required extra work to port SAML profile validation (Attributes, ACS binding edge-cases). Compatibility layer carries risk of prolonged HS256 support — PM committed to client migration timeline. Consider follow-up ticket to replace legacy token endpoints entirely and enforce RS* algorithms by default after Q2 migration window. Also plan an incident-runbook update for key-rotation behavior.
